Wardrobes: measure rail space, door swing and assembly clearance

Compare the inside against the clothes you own

A two- or three-door label does not tell you the split between hanging space and shelves. Check internal rail height, depth and the width of each compartment. Allow enough depth for your hangers and clothing, then check door swing or sliding-door access. A mirror can be useful, but it does not add hanging capacity.

Plan installation before ordering

Check ceiling and floor space needed for the stated assembly method, not just the finished wardrobe height. Read any wall-fixing or restraint instructions and confirm suitable installation arrangements. Check package sizes against stairs and landings and identify the merchant's delivery service. Save the parts list and damage-reporting terms so a missing panel or fitting can be raised clearly.

How this roundup was selected

Our automation searched Rakuten Advertising product feeds belonging to retailers approved for the Worth Buying UK account. Every selected result also had to resolve to a retailer product page that matched the feed product name, and the article required at least 3 validated, region-appropriate results before publication. It did not copy recommendations from the separate Amazon and eBay guide, and it did not create an article when the feed was too limited.

Feed inclusion is not the same as hands-on testing or a guarantee that a product is right for every buyer. Check independent reviews where performance, safety or durability is important.
